from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
from itertools import combinations
import time, sys
n=22
# map edge to var 1..m
edge_var={}
var_edge={}
idx=1
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i+1,n):
        edge_var[(i,j)]=idx; var_edge[idx]=(i,j); idx+=1
m=idx-1
print('vars',m,'5sets',len(list(combinations(range(n),5))))
s=Glucose3()
count=0
start=time.time()
for S in combinations(range(n),5):
    es=[edge_var[(i,j)] for i,j in combinations(S,2)]
    # no red all 0: at least one blue (var true)
    s.add_clause(es)
    # no blue all 1: at least one red (neg)
    s.add_clause([-v for v in es])
    count+=2
print('clauses',count,'build',time.time()-start)
# symmetry break: set colors from vertex 0? maybe assume first 21 edges arbitrary? Could harm. no.
start=time.time()
res=s.solve()
print('res',res,'time',time.time()-start)
if res:
    model=s.get_model()
    val={abs(l): l>0 for l in model if abs(l)<=m}
    sol=[]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i+1,n):
            sol.append(1 if val[edge_var[(i,j)]] else 0)
    print('len',len(sol),'ones',sum(sol))
    print(sol)
    # verify
    bad=[]
    for S in combinations(range(n),5):
        colors=[sol[edge_var[(i,j)]-1] for i,j in combinations(S,2)]
        if all(c==0 for c in colors) or all(c==1 for c in colors): bad.append(S); break
    print('bad',bad[:1])
